chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

We entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) along with Ibn Abi Yafour, and we were a group. So he called for breakfast, and we had breakfast and he had breakfast with us. I was the youngest of the men in age, so I began to be cautious (in my eating) while I was eating. So he said to me: 'Eat! Do you not know that the affection of a man for his brother is recognized by his eating from his food?'

key_terms.أَقْصُرُ: To be cautious or reserve oneself

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of eating together in Shia etiquette?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) underscores the spiritual and social significance of communal dining in Shia tradition, where sharing a single dish symbolizes deep intimacy (mawadda) and equality among companions. It reflects the broader Islamic ethic of breaking bread together to strengthen familial and communal bonds, moving beyond mere sustenance to express genuine affection.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim who said, ‘We went over, along with Ibn Abu Yafour,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and we were a group. So he<sup>asws</sup> called for the breakfast, and we had breakfast and he<sup>asws</sup> had breakfast with us, and I was the youngest of the group in age, so I was cautious in my eating. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Eat (well)! Do you not know that the cordiality of the man for his brother is recognised by his eating from his food?’
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “

Once we along with ibn abu Ya‘fur visited abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and we were a group. Food was prepared and we had lunch. He (the Imam) also took lunch with us. I was the youngest in the group and I made it shorter in my eating. He (the Imam) then said, ’Eat. Did you not know that one’s love for his brother (in belief) comes to light when he eats from his food?”’
